task:
You are a senior product/architecture designer reviewing a notification-routing design for **Anotify**, an open-source self-hostable "Agent notification platform".

PRODUCT CONTEXT:
- An AI Agent finishes a task → POST /v1/notify (API key) → Go backend → pushes notification to the user's devices.
- Device = a notification receiver (currently a browser Web Push subscription). Each device already has: enabled (on/off) and a per-device **status filter** (all / error / success) so e.g. a phone can be set to "only failures".
- The notify payload currently has: title, status (success|error|interrupted|info|warning), body, link, agentId, sessionId, cwd, durationMs, model, priority, ttl, collapseKey, silent, tags, metadata.

NEW REQUIREMENT:
The owner wants **device Tags**. A device can be tagged (e.g. "手机", "工作", "告警"). When the Agent reports a notification it can **choose which tag(s) to send to**, so the notification only reaches devices subscribed to that tag.

YOUR TASK — design a clean, unambiguous routing model:
1. Specify EXACT delivery semantics covering ALL edge cases:
   - notification with NO tags → who receives it?
   - device with NO tags → what does it receive?
   - notification with multiple tags; device with multiple tags → match rule (ANY vs ALL)?
   - should there be a "receive everything" device option, and how does it interact with tags?
2. How does tag-routing interact with the EXISTING per-device status filter (all/error/success)? (Are they independent AND-conditions? Order of evaluation?)
3. Recommend the data model for Device.tags and the notify request field(s).
4. Give 2-3 concrete routing examples that make the semantics obvious.
5. Keep it the SIMPLEST model that is still predictable and covers the owner's use case ("Agent picks a tag, only those devices get it"). Avoid over-engineering.

Be decisive and concrete. Under ~500 words. Design discussion, not code.

criteriaSatisfied.evidence: Returned a concise (<500 word) decisive routing design: single delivery rule covering all edge cases (no-tag notification = broadcast; no-tag device = catch-all; ANY match; exclusivity via tagging all devices), AND-composition with the existing status filter, concrete data model (device.tags JSON array, new deviceTags request field avoiding collision with payload tags), and 3 routing examples; residual risks listed below.

commandsRun.summary: Confirmed prototype structure; no existing deviceTags field, so name is collision-free
Verified subscription shape (raw Web Push + userAgent) and that server already collects per-device delivery results, supporting the observability recommendation

validationOutput: Design discussion only; no code modified. Repo recon used to ground naming and data-model recommendations.
residualRisks: Catch-all semantics: while any untagged device exists, tagged notifications are not strictly exclusive — owner must tag every device for hard partitioning (documented in design)
Notification carrying only unknown/unsubscribed tags may reach zero or only catch-all devices; mitigated by returning per-device delivery results from POST /v1/notify
Case-insensitive tag matching must be applied consistently on both device-write and notify-request paths or CJK/mixed-case tags will silently mismatch
childReport.diffSummary: No diff — design review deliverable only
childReport.manualNotes: Design is intentionally a single rule ('tag filtering activates only when the notification carries tags; untagged device = catch-all') — chosen over strict-partition because it is backward compatible (all-untagged deployments behave exactly as today) and eliminates the dead-letter footgun where an untagged notification matches no device. If the owner later wants hard exclusivity without tagging every device, add an explicit per-device receiveAll boolean and flip untagged-device semantics — a breaking behavioral change, so decide before shipping tags.
